verdict: On original (duplicated) data: split difficulty ranking (easiest to hardest R2) = ['family_disjoint=0.338', 'random=0.256', 'temporal=0.127']. On deduplicated data: ['random=0.649', 'temporal=0.438', 'family_disjoint=0.408']. The temporal split is not family-disjoint (older and newer literature can report the same or closely related compositions), so a high temporal R2 does not contradict the family-disjoint and duplication findings. It addresses a different question: whether a model trained on the literature available at time T predicts the literature that appears after T, which is relevant to prospective screening.
